unite_adi: REGULAR UPPER SECONDARY-YEAR 10-LEVEL: B1.2 THEME 4: FAMILY LIFE & HOME

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students will create a project titled "Family Life and Home," exploring the dynamics of family life across time and cultures. They will begin by describing the daily routines of their family members, comparing these routines to those of previous generations to highlight how roles and responsibilities have evolved. Next, they will focus on hobbies and interests within the family, such as favourite sports or films, and explain how these activities contribute to relations and personal expression. Finally, students will research different types of houses and family structures around the world, comparing them to their own experiences and reflecting on how cultural differences influence family life and home environments. The project should include creative elements such as family interviews, photos, drawings, or videos and will be presented in class. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''family life and home with its components such as family members and their daily routines today and in the past; hobbies and interests of family members (sports & films); different types of houses and families from the world'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student of an upper secondary school in year 10 may know what family life and home, types of houses, family members, their hobbies and their daily routines mean in their own language as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in a foreign language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students in year 10 of an upper secondary school, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''family life and home'' in English from previous themes and/or years such as ''father, mother, brother, sister, a secretary, a security guard, an architect, a mechanic, a clinic, an office,'' and also some structures such as ''What does your father do at the weekends? What does your sister like watching? How does your brother go to school ?'' in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in an upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''family life and home with its components such as family members and their daily routines today and in the past; hobbies and interests of family members (sports & films); different types of houses and families from the world'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a contextual poster or a large picture could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss about the poster and/or the picture in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective : To talk about past and present routines in English through reading skills by using the target vocabulary. Activity 1: Family Routines - Information Gap Reading Students work in groups of 3-4. Each student receives a different part of a reading text about a family’s daily routines today and in the past (e.g., great-grandmother’s routine, sibling’s routine, etc.). The group is also given a blank table with headings like Family Member, Past Routine, and Present Routine. One student, who does not read the text, acts as the recorder and asks questions to the others (e.g., ''What did the great- grandmother use to do in the morning?''). The others share information from their sections to fill in the table collaboratively. As groups work, the teacher moves around, listening to pronunciation and checking the accuracy of responses, and s/he provides supportive feedback. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To compare past and present routines in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity: Past and Present Routines The teacher writes daily routines (e.g., wake up, vacuum the house) on papers and places them in a box. As an example, the teacher picks a paper (e.g., wake up), forms sentences comparing past and present routines using ''used to'' (e.g., ''I used to wake up at 6 am. Now, I wake up at 7 am'') and s/he writes them on the board. Then, students take turns picking a paper, forming similar sentences, and sharing them with the class. The teacher provides constructive and supportive feedback on accuracy and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
